Market watchers had widely expected that the first folding iPhone, set to debut later today, would be named the iPhone Ultra. However, a report yesterday indicated that the device would instead be called the iPhone Duo.

If true, this is an interesting development, as it could mean Apple is holding the "Ultra" suffix for an entirely different future model...

My opinion pieces are speculative by nature, and this one is perhaps even more speculative than most. In terms of actual facts, the only thing we can say for certain is that Apple has used the Ultra label in three contexts, all meaning the top-tier product:

  • Apple Watch Ultra
  • Apple Silicon chips (e.g., M5 Ultra)
  • CarPlay Ultra

There has been speculation that the company plans to extend the Ultra name to a range of new products, expected to include the iPhone Ultra and MacBook Ultra.

Specifically, the iPhone Ultra name was reported to be destined for the foldable phone being unveiled later today. But as of yesterday, we're expecting it to be called the iPhone Duo — what's going on? I can think of three possibilities.

1. The least interesting reason

The least interesting explanation is that Apple isn't using the Ultra label because the foldable phone is not the top-tier iPhone. It's a device with unique features, but it is expected to be inferior to the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in several respects. If all the reports are correct, it won't have a variable aperture lens on the main camera, nor a telephoto lens; no Face ID; and battery life will also be less than the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

So logically, it shouldn't be called the iPhone Ultra. But Apple doesn't always follow logic when it comes to product naming — for example, the 2015 MacBook Air was heavier than the 12-inch MacBook, and the 2022 Mac Studio outperformed the Mac Pro. So while this is a possible explanation, it's certainly not definitive.

2. Ultra will be the 20th anniversary model

Another related possibility is that the iPhone Ultra name is being saved for the 20th anniversary model expected next year, taking another step toward the long-rumored "a single piece of glass" vision. If it combines the sleekest design with iPhone Pro capabilities, then it would truly be worthy of the name.

3. Something even bigger is in the works

The most exciting possibility is that, after Apple unveils the "single piece of glass" (iPhone Glass?), it won't stop there and add a brand-new member to the iPhone family, with the iPhone Ultra name reserved for an entirely different model — one that is truly top-of-the-line in every respect.

I won't speculate on what form it will take, but it probably won't surprise anyone that my own expectations would focus on significantly improved camera capabilities, starting with a much larger image sensor.

What do you think? Which of the three explanations do you find most likely? Or do you have a better idea of your own? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
